utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, this is case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Gaynor, are you ready to call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We are, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Thank you, Your Honour. There's just two quick matters I want to place on the record before we proceed. Firstly, I'd like to thank the Prosecution and the Trial Chamber for allowing the evidence in chief and the cross-examination to be split up in such a way on Thursday and Friday and I do appreciate that in view of the timetable I'm currently undertaking and I'd like to place that on the record. Thank you for that indulgence, firstly. And secondly, we have with us a part-time intern that we've had for the last time, Mr. Kevin Afghani who is on his way back to Texas and this is his last day with us and his present is coming to court today to assist me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Afghani that is therefore a welcome and farewell occasion. Welcome in court. Mr. Gaynor, next witness, protective measures in place are voice distortion, face distortion, and pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Gaynor, in view of the questions you are going to put to the witness first, should we start in open session, should we start in private session? I take it that the first exhibit that you will present to him will be his pseudonym sheet and then ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, I suggest we begin in open session with some preliminary matters and then the public summary and then we turn to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom. Madam Registrar already assigns a number to the pseudonym sheet which saves time later.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The pseudonym sheet will be Prosecution Exhibit P635, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness 132. From your response, I understand that you can hear me in a language you understand.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 132, we'll not use your name. We'll address you by using this number, 132. Your face will not be visible for the outside world and your voice will be distorted when your testimony will be sent to the outside world. If there's any need, since your testimony might deal with identifying data, we can turn into private session so that even the content of your testimony under those circumstances will remain unknown to the outside world. I ask you to stand and -- before giving evidence in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration. The text is handed out to you now by Madam Usher. Could you please make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly swear that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated. You will first be examined by Mr. Gaynor, counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Witness 132, in a moment we're going to show you a piece of paper on which is written your name and your date of birth and I would be grateful if you could confirm simply with yes or no that that is your name and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 132
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd now request that the witness be shown his two witness statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, have you received them and have...? Could you assign exhibit numbers. First, to the ICTY witness statement of 26 of January, 1999.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The statement dated 26 January 1999 will be P636, and the statement dated 29 April 2003 will be P637.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask the usher just to move the ELMO a little bit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sir, have you had an opportunity to carefully review those two documents over the last couple of days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 132
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And subject to some corrections which we'll make in the course of the proceedings today, do you adopt those two documents for the purpose of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 132
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd now like to read a short summary for the public of the matters which are contained in those statements. In his statement, the witness refers to an SDS rally in Doboj in August or September 1990, attended by Radovan Karadzic, Velibor Ostojic, Nikola Koljevic, and other SDS representatives. At this rally, the witness heard several speakers make references to the Serbs remaining on their land and all Serbs living in one country. At the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992, weapons were distributed to Serb civilians in villages all over Doboj municipality by the JNA. The SDS established a Crisis Staff in Doboj. The SDS president in Doboj was Milan Ninkovic. In January and February 1992, Arkan's and Seselj's troops started arriving in the area. Checkpoints were erected and manned by Serb soldiers. Prior to the takeover of Doboj by Serb forces, 10 to 15 non-Serb shops and kiosks were destroyed. There were no attacks on Serb shops. Some Muslims were killed. On the 3rd of May, 1992, the Serbs took control of Doboj. The Serb army and police occupied all government and public institutions. Muslim policemen were arrested. The Serb Crisis Staff took control of the municipality. Vehicles equipped with loudspeakers were driven around the town; demands were broadcast from the loudspeakers that any Bosniaks and Croats with weapons had to hand them in. The announcements also said that Doboj had become Serbian Doboj and that Serbian liberation units had freed Doboj. During the takeover, Arkan's men, Seselj's men, JNA reserve soldiers, and the local police were all involved in some way, for example, by occupying buildings, setting up checkpoints, or standing guard. The army had installed artillery positions in more than 10 positions around Doboj town. The witness and other Muslims decided to leave the town. That ends the summary. I request, Your Honour, that we go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn it to closed session -- private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Witness as your evidence deals primarily with Doboj municipality, I'm going to show you a couple of maps now. I would request that the book of maps are placed on the ELMO at page 2. Sir, I'd request you to point to the municipality of Doboj to your right. If you look to your right on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 132
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in your statement, you've made several mentions, this is in paragraph 2, that Doboj has been -- always been considered to be a very important strategic location. Now, you mentioned the fact that it's -- that there are a number of rivers that meet in Doboj. Are there any other reasons why Doboj was considered to occupy a strategic location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 132
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you please give us some of those reasons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 132
utterances.text: Doboj was the largest railway junction in the former Yugoslavia. Also, almost all roads running from the west towards the south and from the south towards the east pass through Doboj. In times of war, for example, in 1992, there is Mount Ozren dominating over the entire territory of Doboj municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And what is the significance of Mount Ozren?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 132
utterances.text: Mount Ozren is located between several municipalities in central Bosnia. It's very important strategically in time of war. It was even important in World War II because during 1945, the partisan units liberated that area. It is still very important today in that part of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. We're now going to show you a map of the city of Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: At this stage, I'd like to explain to Your Honours that the witness has marked this map with a yellow line and in the course of his testimony we'll come to the significance of this yellow line. We're just bringing the map in at this stage for orientation reasons. I'd request when the registrar has a moment, an exhibit number for this map.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The map will be P638. Does it need to be under seal, Mr. Gaynor?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It does not need to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could you point out, just very briefly, the train station.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Counsel please switch off his microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd request the usher to move the map up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 132
utterances.text: It's this part here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And do you know the locations of mosques in Doboj town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 132
utterances.text: Yes. One of the mosques is somewhere here. This is the upper mosque here, and there's one here. There was a mosque here as well. And there was another mosque in Orasje up here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We'll turn to a map a little later on in your testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor, if the witness points a at something on the map, you should describe where he points it because otherwise one could not understand the testimony without consulting the videotapes. Let me just -- the witness first pointed close to where it's indicated on the map one-third from above, approximately in the middle where it says, "mosque"; then he pointed at a place just north of where the map says "building"; and the third one -- and when I say "building," building 198M, 51M because there are more buildings on it; and then the third one was a little bit east from that. Certainly, if you are preparing such maps, it saves a lot of time if you ask the witness to indicate with numbers where mosques are. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Certainly. Thank you, Your Honours. This specific map, just for everyone's attention has a legend on the right-hand side which shows mosques and churches which is -- which will be helpful in reviewing the witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but at the same time, the witness pointed at a place where there was a mosque and where there's no mosque anymore as far as I understand, where there's no indication of a mosque in accordance with the agenda. So for mosques that have disappeared, it's hardly of any use to look at the agenda. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We can put the map to one side now, thank you. Sir, in your statement and this is at paragraph 8, you said that you were aware of the policies of various political parties. You said that the SDS platform was based on the establishment of a state where all Serbs could live together. Now, how did you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 132
utterances.text: Well, as a deputy in the republican parliament of Bosnia and Herzegovina, especially after the adoption of the memorandum, the letter of understanding, and our decision to carry out a referendum in Bosnia and Herzegovina, they said that the Serbs should all live together in one state and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I request that the witness be shown the exhibit, please. And I'd request an exhibit number for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Prosecution Exhibit P639.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, as is -- can be seen, this is a set of decisions by local communes in Doboj municipality. Some are dated the 13th of October, 1991; some are dated the 14th of October, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sir, you've had an opportunity to review these decisions before today; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 132
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court what these decisions are about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 132
utterances.text: These decisions concern the demand of the Main Board of the Doboj SDS to all municipalities that they should declare the territories of their local communes an integral part of the state of Yugoslavia rather than Bosnia and Herzegovina. What is very important to point out here is that this document shows that the SDS, or rather its Municipal Board, used the rights of the local communes because they were self-governing bodies and they had to carry out only the decisions of the Municipal Assembly, not those of a political party. And yet this applied to all the local communes in Doboj municipality, as you can see from the stamps here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd now request that the witness be shown the next exhibit, please. I'd request an exhibit number for that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The exhibit number will be P640.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: These are some of the decisions of the communes in Doboj dated the 13th of October, 1991 and these include three that we've just seen. The difference is that these bear a stamp of the SDS indicating -- possibly indicating receipt by the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just in relation to that, this is a matter in which Mr. Gaynor really shouldn't be giving evidence from the bar table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, are you opposing against Mr. Gaynor saying that the stamp of the SDS appears or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I mean there really isn't a -- that is not in the nature of a question to the witness, that is in the nature of an assertion by the questioner. And it is on that basis that I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, that stamps appear on these documents from the SDS is something even without any questions the Chamber could deduce from the paper itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Precisely, Your Honour, it is a matter for the Chamber and it's not a matter for editorialising in a question from the Prosecutor. That's my point. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see what question then follows. If the question is about the stamp then of course it might be wise to draw the attention of the witness to the presence of the stamp. Please proceed, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the best way to proceed is we can move on to the next exhibit. Your Honours can draw which ever inferences Your Honours wish from that exhibit. I would request therefore that the next exhibit be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that would be, Madam Registrar, P641 -- no, again I'm -- I leave it to you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That was correct, the next exhibit number is P641.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: This is a letter headed "Serb Democratic Party, BiH, SDS Municipal Board, Doboj." And I'll ask the witness:

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sir, could you explain what this document means.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, just in relation to this, this is a document in relation to the evidence that is not the witness's document; it is not in fact a document that he can, in reality, cast any light on. The document speaks for itself. It's a document that the Trial Chamber can deal with at the relevant time and draw whatever inferences it wishes. But to question this witness on a document of this nature does not, in my submission, assist the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Gaynor, could you first find out whether the witness is familiar with this document, how he became familiar with it, and whether he dealt with it in a way which would ask him to interpret that. If it's just a matter of reading and -- then perhaps we should put different questions to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: There's one small procedural question. I would request that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will then turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Witness, we're moving on to a new topic and that is the arming of Serb civilians in Doboj. In your statement - there's no need to refer to it, it's paragraph 16 for the rest of the Court - you said in your statement at the end of 1991 and at the beginning of 1992, weapons were distributed to Serb civilians in villages all over Doboj municipality by the JNA from the central barracks. There's no need, sir, for you to refer to your statement, it's quite all right. My question is: How did you become aware that this distribution of weapons was taking place across the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 132
utterances.text: As I said in my statement, there was a local commune, Ritesic, which was of mixed ethnicity. In one part there lived Serbs and Croats lived in the other part. And the Serb representatives came to see me one day from this local commune and they said, or rather the Croats came to explain that weapons had been distributed only to the Serbs. The entire council of this local commune came to see me. Secondly, as I said, the president of Maglaj, a lady, also personally asked that Cazim Hadzic, the commander of the garrison to intervene because a day or two previously, she had seen in villages in the Maglaj municipality that weapons were being distributed to Serb civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would request that we go into private session out of an abundance of caution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn it to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, in your statement, you said that you saw - this is paragraph 23 - you saw Seselj's and Arkan's men during the takeover. Is it, in fact, correct that you did see Seselj's men during the takeover but you heard of the involvement of Arkan's men from other persons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 132
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 24, you say, "Bijeljina, Visegrad, Foca, Bratunac, and other towns in eastern Bosnia were already taken over by Serbs. I knew what had happened in those places." My first question is what was it you knew? What had happened in those places?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 132
utterances.text: The first attack on one of the Bosnian cities was on Bijeljina. This was carried out by the Arkan's men, the paramilitaries. A few days ago, there was a trial of a person or rather a person attended a trial. He was a journalist who covered these developments along with Madam Plavsic and others. We learned later on that it had been launched by Arkan. Later on, all the developments in towns where people were abused, stories about this went around, people talked about it, and one could also learn about this on the TV.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I want to focus there on specifically in the period prior to the takeover of Doboj. You said that you could learn about it on the TV. What, briefly, did you see on the television about events in eastern Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 132
utterances.text: The Sarajevo TV that broadcast on several occasions, these were reports made by our journalists who went out into the field to report on what was going on. Many could not even reach these areas because there was an exodus of people leaving Bijeljina who were eyewitnesses and they were interviewed on the TV and they talked about how the Bosniaks had been abused. Particularly memorable was an interview with a lady from Bratunac who said that she saw in several houses in her street dead bodies of her neighbours who had been killed and she had also heard that all the residents living in that particular street had been killed in their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: What ethnicity --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just in relation to the sort of evidence we're receiving at the moment, I do object to further questions on what was seen on TV. I think this witness is here to tell us about what he knows about Doboj and it's not particularly helpful to the Trial Chamber to learn secondhand what this man saw on TV.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, what people saw on the television at that time, whether it was the truth or whether it was a manipulation of media certainly may have influenced the behaviour of people at that time. So I do agree that -- with you that you if you see something on television, then that's not true for that reason; but at the same time, what people saw on television -- to see something on television is a fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Oh, indeed, Your Honour, and I don't disagree with that but if we spend a lot of time dealing with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well Mr. Gaynor is not going to spend a lot of time on it, I take it. Mr. Gaynor, I take it that the general impression would do on the basis of what I said because if I see something on television to happen, then it does not necessarily mean that it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And other evidence of course in terms of Bijeljina have been presented. And so therefore, I take it that Mr. Gaynor is leading this evidence in order to find out whether the behaviour of persons in other municipalities might have been influenced by they saw on television and therefore it's important to know what approximately they saw on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'd just like to add that one of the issues in dispute is the extent to which the commission of crimes was publicly known and reflected in the media.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps this is not a matter that should be dealt with whilst the witness is present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I -- as a matter of fact, I would allow Mr. Gaynor within the limits I gave, and of course having heard the last line he spoke, to continue. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sir, you have referred there briefly to a broadcast of a woman in Bratunac. Could you clarify the ethnicity of that woman.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 132
utterances.text: She was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Did you hear on the radio or did you read in any newspapers prior to the 3rd of May, 1992 any reference to killings of Muslims or destruction of Muslim property of any kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 132
utterances.text: Doboj was attacked on the 3rd of May. Before that, those towns Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that I mentioned in eastern Bosnia had already fallen. There were residents leaving those areas just as the residents of Doboj were leaving the area after the takeover and of course they were not leaving of their own free will or going on vacation, they were driven out of there and they talked about it. Fortunately, Doboj did not suffer as much as a town as did others in Bosnia and Herzegovina. If this was the case of just one person watching this on the TV or just watching one person leaving, then this might be disputed; however, if you have 15.000 people leaving an area, then it is quite clear what we are talking about. The alternative for these people was to be put away in camps as was the case in some other towns.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is the problem with that sort of generalised question about reading newspapers and what have you. Your Honour, this sort of evidence in relation to what was going on in other parts of Bosnia is a matter for the Trial Chamber and is not going to be assisted by the witness giving this sort of evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I wondered whether you would like to respond to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. First of all there's two very clear points here. One is knowledge of the accused, did he know the crimes were being committed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is just not an appropriate matter to be discussed in the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Gaynor, of course it's not. We are not going to present in the presence of the witness what the real issues are. Ms. Loukas, let me say it in a different way. You may object to any question put by Mr. Gaynor if you think fit to do so. You said that this evidence was problematic which is not an objection. Mr. Gaynor, you may proceed but at the same time, you now are aware of what Ms. Loukas finds problematic so therefore, try to avoid that she has to object. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, sir, in your statement, you said, "To avoid destruction, I advised the Bosniak --" at this point, I request that we go into private session, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn it to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, any need to put further questions to the witness raised by questions of the Bench?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, there are two points that I need to make. And firstly, it's in relation to Your Honour's questions. I want to make this point first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, I would first like to know from you whether you will put any questions to the witness because if not, you can make whatever observations you'd like to but then the witness could be excused and could --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour, then in that case, I can indicate that no, I do not propose to ask the witness any further questions; and my second point is to raise these other matters for Your Honour. But I'm happy for Your Honour to bring the witness back in, excuse him, and then I can place the matters on the record that I need to place on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's exactly what I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, the situation is even more complicated since Judge Canivell has one more question for the witness. So Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom. Ms. Loukas, may I take it that the question -- questions by Judge Canivell would make you reconsider your position as to not further put your questions to the witness that you report to me without asking, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Welcome back, Witness 132. Judge Canivell has one or more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Canivell doubts whether he took the wrong channel but...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: I was hearing in French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Everything is fine now, again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: I'm going to address you in English. And my point is the next. You said in your statement that those paramilitary forces, Arkan's and Seselj's forces, arrived to stay in Doboj in January/February 1992. Nevertheless, the takeover of the town by the Serb forces didn't happen until May the 3rd, 1992. Can you tell me what were doing those paramilitary people, that is at the moment that you said they were 500 strong, why they were staying there because the only -- the only thing we know, we have been told for sure is that the Seselj's people were going to the army barracks for their meals but for the rest, they were remain in -- what were they doing during these three months March, April, perhaps you said that they began arriving on January, these three months, what they were doing there besides this activity of maintaining themselves in life?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 132
utterances.text: It wasn't the 3rd of March but the 3rd of May, 1992, up to the 3rd of May. There was already a war theatre in Podnovlje, some 20 kilometres away from Doboj. And the JNA, even from the Tuzla area, would come there and send soldiers off to war. This is illustrated best by the fall of Bijeljina. Bijeljina was completely occupied by Arkan's units alone and this was before Doboj fell. As for Seselj's men, 500 of them probably did not arrive all at once. They were seen sleeping in the Serbian church in Doboj and it was only some 15 days before the attack on Doboj that they expelled the people in the weekend cottages in the area of Ankare and there they encamped themselves waiting for the 3rd of May. On the 3rd of May, they attacked together with the regular army of the Bosnian Serbs which was still called the JNA at the time but had been ethnically cleansed of all other ethnicities but the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: Perhaps -- may we understand that those people began arriving on January/February but not the 500 of them and they arrived later on or what was that? Because I don't understand what so many people were doing stationed there without moving only except for they went to have meals in a different location. Perhaps they were -- you said that they were in Bijeljina. But if they were in Bijeljina, they were withdrew or they were so many as to be -- quite a few in Bijeljina and 500 more are still in Doboj? How can you explain this situation? I would like to know better about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 132
utterances.text: When I said starting in January, that's when groups of Seselj's men were first observed in houses in Serb local communes. I don't know what they were doing. Were they going off to fight in the Podnovlje area, down there, I don't know. But on the 3rd of May in Doboj, they did participate in the takeover of Doboj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CANIVELL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If there are no further questions, I'd like to thank you, Witness 132 to come to The Hague. The Defence will not cross-examine you, they have no questions for you. That means that this concludes your testimony in this Court. I'd like to thank you for -- usually I say having answered questions of both parties, but at least to have answered all questions put to you in this courtroom and I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Loukas. You would like to put something on the record. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. As I foreshadowed, it's in relation to Your Honour's questions and as Your Honour is aware, I've placed on the record before that of course this is a hybrid system and the Judges asks questions in a way that is not the usual practice in a common-law system but nevertheless we are in a hybrid system and as a result matters that I would normally object to at a judge asking questions are taken with a somewhat greater level of discretion because the test that has been enunciated is only in exceptional circumstances as Your Honour as indicated, only in exceptional circumstances. Now, Your Honour, in relation to -- of course, the background being that leading questions are -- on critical areas, are prohibited as a general rule because the fact is the court requires the evidence from the witness and there's a danger in suggesting answers to a witness. That the much is clear and that much is abundantly clear to everybody in the courtroom. But when a question is asked in a leading fashion or suggestive of an answer with the imprimatur of the Judge, a fortiori it's an even more exceptional situation. Now in relation to the questions that were asked of this witness, I would indicate the vast bulk of them being questions of an open nature, I have no submission or objection to make in relation to them. But specifically in relation to a question that appeared on page 62 of the transcript, Your Honour, and this was this question of the meals and what have you, and the witness very clearly gave his answer on page 19 and 20 of the transcript in his evidence in chief on this issue. Then Your Honour picked up the issue in your questions and very specifically here, on page 62, Your Honour has indicated in your question: "But at least some people in the regular forces must have known." Now, Your Honour, it's specifically that that I object to. And with the greatest of respect, Your Honour, that suggestion in the question is what I object to because the temptation for the witness to agree with a suggestion with the imprimatur of the Judge is overwhelming. And Your Honour will notice the different in the answers of this witness initially in evidence in chief, the series of questions prior to Your Honour asking this question, and then Your Honour's question with that suggestion of "must have known." And Your Honour, I very clearly and specifically do place any objection in relation to questions that contain that sort of suggestion in them from the Bench. That's the matter I wish to place on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Loukas. Mr. Gaynor, is there any procedural issue you'd like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We have no submissions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No submissions at this point. Ms. Loukas, I've got one question for you at this moment. You ask a specific matter to be struck from the record whereas some follow-up questions came up which might, to some extent, have changed your view. I'm trying to find it. I don't know whether you remember that you asked.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: At what page of the transcript?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just finding it because I was on the right page but then I wanted to go to the page that you mentioned so I'll find it quickly. Yes. It is on page 23. Some questions were put, as a matter of fact, you responded to the answer of the witness -- just in relation to that last answer, you said, "A portion of that second-last answer was not actually a specific answer to the question and he was also Serb and they probably did not want to shed any light on --"

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, that's a quote from -- that probably should be in a quote, actually, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But apart from that, you wanted that part to be struck whereas Mr. Gaynor did put some follow-up questions which gave it at least a context.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I'm just reading the further questions and answers, Your Honour, just to place it in context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness said that they probably did not want to shed any light on these incidents and of course what he then did at a later stage was giving a lot of explanation what gave him reasons to even if put in the form of conclusion, to believe that no serious attention was paid to the investigation of such matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour, and there was a series of questions that were also asked there by His Honour Judge Hanoteau in relation to the issue. In view of the fact that there have been those various follow-up questions and the matter has been explored, I now withdraw my application to strike that particular portion because the matter was explored in a way that it needed to be explored subsequently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that we don't have to decide on that. It also learns that one thing: That requests to have parts of the evidence struck from the record very often should not be decided on that very moment, that sometimes you would first have to see what context it get, what other evidence is presented because only at a totally different stage you could really come to conclusions as to whether that evidence is totally useless.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. As with everything, it's something of a balancing exercise and of course, Your Honours, we've had situations where Your Honour has in fact struck something from the record and it was very appropriate at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not saying it's never appropriate but very often -- I mean, if you want to balance things, sometimes you first need to have something on both scales and to wait for a while to see whether there will be any weight on the other part of the scale.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I guess I always have an instinctive reaction to speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then this brings me to a second observation. Once you also objected to a question put by Mr. Gaynor and before the answer was given, you knew already that the answer would be secondhand hearsay whereas from the answer, it appeared that it was just firsthand hearsay. Of course firsthand hearsay is still hearsay, but I think that sometimes it's wise to just wait a second and see what happens. I think that usually the results of taking a bit more time are less dramatic before a professional bench as they would have been before a jury. Mr. Gaynor, a similar matter for you. You asked extensively on the 15.000, how it was composed, whether there were -- and the witness said that they came from Derventa, they were refugees, they were Muslims, they were Croats. If you had looked 10 pages earlier, you would see that you put exactly the same questions to the witness and that the witness gave exactly the same answers. For your guidance, that was on page 14, line 17. Are there any -- oh, yes, and one final thing, Ms. Loukas. You made on objection and -- about question asked, question answered. And it will not take more than two minutes since we have this time, let's use it to see whether we can improve our court performance. You raised an issue of question asked and question answered. I invited you to tell me exactly where that specific question was asked; then you pointed at the question which was a more general question on the same subject. I then gave a decision of the Chamber that Mr. Gaynor was entitled to put a follow-up question asking whether the reasons given were the exclusive reasons or whether they were more and then you said, "Yes that's the point, that's a leading question." I try not only to study the hybrid system but I also try to get as good as I can acquainted with the common-law tradition. I must say, but you will certainly assist me if it's different, I did not find anywhere until this moment how an objection of question asked, question answered undergoes a change of character and that at the end of an objection introduced under this heading, this Chamber would have to decide on leading questions which is, of course, a totally different matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I see Your Honour's point. I will make one comment in relation to that. In fact, as often there is with many objections, there's a main point of the objection and there's a subsidiary point and in the interests of brevity I went for my main point but that doesn't mean that there may not be a -- there are questions, of course, Your Honour, that have a number of bases that they can be objected to and one tends to take the headline or the one that you think is the most pernicious aspect of the question asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which unfortunately was without factual basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]... and it reminds me that of course that I must always accept Your Honour's judgement on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn until -- exhibits still to be dealt with. Madam Registrar, we do indeed, we have the -- yes, we just go through the numbers, you mentioned numbers and we'll give a decision on admission.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P635 to P637, under seal. P638 to P641.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then Mr. Gaynor, as far as P638 is concerned, -- no, 639, you have described it as a set of decisions dated the 14th but that should be the 13th or the 14th, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So Madam Registrar, I take it that you will make the set consisting of two dates rather than of one. No objections. The P635 up until and including 641 are admitted into evidence. If there are no further procedural issues, we'll adjourn until next Monday morning in this same courtroom at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 25th day of April, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.26 p.m.
